description:
IdentityError::MalformedInput is returned from at least the following distinct conditions:

ServerName::dns_name failures:
  1. empty input
  2. bare '.'
  3. contains '*' (wildcard in target)
  4. label too long (> 63)
  5. total name too long (> 253)
  6. hyphen at label start/end
  7. non-LDH ASCII byte
  8. embedded empty label ('foo..bar')
  9. IDNA 2008 conversion failure

ServerName::ip_address failures:
  10. empty
  11. contains '%' (zone id)
  12. IPv6 parse failure (any sub-cause)
  13. IPv4 parse failure (any sub-cause, including leading-zero rejection vs out-of-range vs wrong octet count)
  14. unmatched '[' bracket

MailboxName::parse failures:
  15. missing '@'
  16. empty local or domain
  17. double '@'
  18. whitespace / NUL / quote / angle-bracket in local
  19. ASCII local-part not atext
  20. ASCII local-part has leading/trailing/consecutive dots
  21. domain fails the same DNS validation as above

Caller impact: a TLS service receiving 'bad input' from a user-supplied SNI string cannot tell from IdentityError::MalformedInput whether to:

* log 'invalid hostname syntax' and 400 the request,
* warn 'IDN conversion failed; is the user trying punycode?',
* alert 'asterisk in supposedly-target name suggests config injection',
* etc.

For prelaunch architectural completeness, IdentityError should subdivide. Suggested non-exhaustive variant shape:

  MalformedDnsName { reason: DnsNameError }
  MalformedIp { reason: IpAddressError }
  MalformedMailbox { reason: MailboxError }

with structured reason enums (also #[non_exhaustive]) carrying the specific failure mode. This is the shape pyca/cryptography's exceptions take, and rustls-pki-types subdivides similarly.

Lower-effort alternative: add variants like InvalidWildcardInTarget, LabelTooLong, NotLdh, IdnaFailure, IpZoneIdUnsupported, MailboxLocalPartMalformed, MailboxDomainMalformed, while keeping the existing MalformedInput as a #[deprecated] alias-by-not-being-returned.

Severity P2: catchable error subdivisions can be added non-breakingly later because the enum is #[non_exhaustive], but only by adding *new* variants, never by removing MalformedInput. So shipping coarse and refining later is feasible — file as P2 'should fix before 1.0 to avoid double-coverage forever'.
title: IdentityError::MalformedInput too coarse — collapses ≥10 distinct failure modes
